messages:
Janet S.: Heads up — ACME reported a big drop in embeddings throughput this morning. tokens/sec looks normal but vectors/sec is ~60% lower. :thinking_face:

Kevin S.: ugh. Any error codes from their requests? dimension mismatches?

Janet S.: No 4xx. Most requests are 200 but take much longer. We see queue_depth spike on their tenant route. GPU util at 95% on nodes serving embed-large-v2.

Maria G.: Can you paste a short example request payload (sanitized)?

Janet S.: simple call they shared: 
```json
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "embed-large-v2",
  "input": ["some short sentence"],
  "client_meta": { "batch_hint": 128 }
}
```
No dimension field in payload (we infer).

Olivia R.: That batch_hint seems suspect. Our batching controller uses batch_hint to influence windowing for dedicated customers. If their hint jumped up recently it could create huge batches and cause queueing.

Kevin S.: Did we ship any batching/window changes? @infra-bot show last deploy for batch-controller

infra-bot: deploy-log: batch-controller v3.7.0 deployed 2026-02-18 03:12 UTC by jsmith — changed default window_ms from 20 -> 60 for latency optimization.

Josh R.: default window -> 60ms explains larger batch sizes; that would increase GPU batch sizes for embeddings and could push kernels into a slower code path or evict kv caches more often. But why tokens/sec is unchanged?

Maria G.: embeddings requests have low token counts (1-2). tokens/sec metric came from text-gen pipeline; different route. So tokens/sec staying ok is expected. We need vectors/sec specifically.

Janet S.: Repro plan from support: run load test hitting embed-large-v2 with small inputs, replicate batch_hint present/absent. Can eng reproduce locally?

Kevin S.: I can run a quick local micro-benchmark. Steps:
1) start single GPU instance with embed-large-v2 (quantized variant)
2) run 2 RPS -> record vectors/sec, queue depth, gpu_util
3) run 200 RPS with batch_hint=128 vs batch_hint=1
4) toggle controller window param to 20ms and 60ms

Olivia R.: Also capture kernel selection logs. Use env DEBUG_KERNEL=1 to log chosen kernels and code path names.

Josh R.: I ran step 2/3 on a dev instance: with window=60ms batch sizes avg=48, gpu_util=96%, vectors/sec dropped 58%. With window=20ms avg batch=12, gpu_util=68%, vectors/sec normal. Kernel logs show fallback to "int8-blocked" path when batch >32 for this quantized model.

Maria G.: So hypothesis: the newer window causes larger batches which trigger a suboptimal kernel for this quantized variant. That kernel reduces vectors/sec even though it increases token throughput per-GPU in other workloads.

Janet S.: Customer-specific: ACME uses dedicated route with `batch_hint` set by their SDK. Could be a recent SDK change. @Kevin S. can you share a repro script we can run against staging to validate rollback?

Kevin S.: Pushing quick repro script to thread:
```bash
# run load against staging embed route
for rps in 2 50 200; do
  hey -n $((rps*60)) -c $rps -q 1 -m POST \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY" \
    -D payload.json https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
done
```
payload.json contains single short sentences. Set header `X-Client-Batch-Hint` to 128 to mimic ACME.
```
# kernel debug (on runtime host)
export DEBUG_KERNEL=1 && tail -f /var/log/runtime/kernels.log | grep embed-large-v2
```

Olivia R.: Also captured metric screenshot from prod route (pasted inline): avg_batch_size jumped from 10 -> 46 at 03:15 UTC and vectors/sec dropped concurrently.

Janet S.: We should offer ACME a mitigation: set tenant override to cap batch_size at 16 or roll back window to 20ms for their pool. Which is fastest?

Josh R.: Tenant override is safer and quick (no global rollback). I can push cap=16 for ACME pool — needs 10m maintenance window but no downtime.

Maria G.: Before doing that, confirm no regressions for other customers who benefited from 60ms default. Maybe apply cap only to pools using quantized embed-large-v2.

Kevin S.: I applied a temporary cap to acme-pool: max_batch_size=16. Monitoring now.

infra-bot: config-change: acme-pool max_batch_size set to 16 by kevin_s at 2026-03-10T10:42:40Z

Janet S.: ACME reports vectors/sec back to expected within 4m. They sent logs showing p99 latency down from 2.1s -> 0.6s. :tada:

Olivia R.: Action items:
- Josh: add kernel quality test for batch sizes >32 for quantized embed-large-v2 (owner: Josh, ETA: 2 days)
- Maria: add a per-model compatibility matrix that flags when window changes can cause kernel fallbacks (owner: Maria, ETA: 5 days)
- Kevin: follow up with SDK team to stop sending aggressive batch_hint or make it bounded by route policy (owner: Kevin, ETA: 3 days)

Josh R.: I'll also add an alert rule: if avg_batch_size > 30 and vectors/sec drops >30% then fire a paging alert to eng-ml.

Janet S.: Closing loop with ACME: scheduled follow-up call in 48h. Thanks all.

Kevin S.: notes: root cause = default batching window increase combined with client-supplied batch_hint -> large batches -> kernel fallback for quantized embed-large-v2 -> vectors/sec regression while tokens/sec unaffected.

Maria G.: Putting a short postmortem doc in #postmortems after owner writeup.

infra-bot: incident-note: temporary tenant cap applied; customer throughput recovered.
